title: Criteria attack evaluation catalogue
description: The manifest of the cases that evaluate the attack lenses. Each case is a defective document and its control, or a control alone, kept in a directory named by the case's ID beside this manifest, under a directory named cases. A case the evaluation contract's catalogue table lists must state that row's served parents, rule, lens and child exactly; a case the table does not list, such as one harvested from a real round, is held to every other check.

id.description: The case's ID, which also names its directory, so it is a bare name that cannot lead out of the cases directory.

serves.description: What the case serves: each parent criterion ID the catalogue table's Serves cell names, and each what-if question it quotes, written without its quotation marks. The table's other prose in that cell describes the defect and is not stated here, so a row naming no criterion and quoting no question serves an empty list. A row covering a range of cases gives each case the parent IDs it names and one of its quoted questions, in order. The comparison ignores order.

rule.description: The rule ID of the acceptance-criteria standard the case's defect breaks, as the table writes it without backticks. The value none marks a control-only case, which plants no defect and so breaks no rule.

lens.description: The lens that owns the rule and attacks the case. For a pair case it must enforce the rule, as the lens's own front matter states. A control-only case states the table's value, full panel.

child.description: The evaluation contract's criterion that this case passing discharges, as the table's Child column states it. A row covering a range of cases gives each case one criterion of its range, in order.

site.description: Where the defect sits: the ID of the criterion it is planted in, or none when the defect is an absence. A control-only case has no defect and states null.

detection.description: One sentence stating what an objection must say to detect the defect.

source_revision.description: The revision a harvested document was taken from, or null for a document written for the catalogue.
